what_happened: The adequacy half's computational core already exists in-tree and is language-agnostic: WitnessFamily/Sharing/Fulfil.lean's AUFix (step/iter/lfp/mem_lfp_iff/lfp_induction at an arbitrary vertex type with a Finset-valued successor and two Bool predicates, mentioning no formula), plus BiLasso/GoodCycle.lean's good-cycle extraction with an explicit cycleBound, plus PlusWitnessFamily's (C2') PlusThreadFulfilling and (C5) StabFaithful. The round therefore does not need to invent the fulfilment machinery.

The adequacy-gap probe compiled clean on the first attempt (exit 0, no errors, no warnings, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] on all nine theorems). The unfulfilled cycle was derived on paper from the Hintikka biconditionals before any Lean was written, by taking the eighteenth probe's non-vacuity types and flipping ev.neg to ev (which forces evnn in, dd in, chi out), so no decide-driven search was needed.

The plan's 18-theorem Lean Challenge block was compiled through lake env lean at plan time (exit 0, 18 sorry warnings, no other diagnostic), so every pinned signature is known to elaborate before implementation starts; the fixture layer was ported byte-for-byte from the already-compiling eighteenth and twentieth probes, which concentrated all elaboration risk in the 18 new signatures.

First compile of the Challenge block failed on one Decidable synthesis: the box clause written as a nested iff under two Finset binders (decide (forall x in R, forall psi in closure, isBox psi -> (psi in x.2.1 <-> forall y in R, argOf psi in y.2.1))) would not synthesize. Resolved by pushing the inner universal into its own decide and comparing Bools, and by factoring the stab clause into a named stabOk helper; recompiled to exit 0. The same shape is the first thing the implementer will hit on the stab/box fields, so the Challenge block pins the working form.
